newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down 10 bps to 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down 10 bps to 10.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate eased 10 basis points to 12.3 percent on Friday, amid a relatively high supply of kuna funds.
Daily demand for kuna funds was met in full, totalling 44.9 million, and 25 million kuna were left on the supply side.
New loans accounted for 33.2 million kuna. Most were call money borrowings granted at a steady 10.5 percent.
"But in the second part of the day one call-money loan was struck at 9.5 percent and we also concluded a one-week loan at 9.5 percent, and that lowered the weighted rate," a dealer told Reuters.
Other term loans were granted at rates ranging between 11 percent for one-week funds and 18 percent for one-month borrowings.
Banks extended old loans at 9.4, 14 and 15 percent for one-week, two-week and one-month borrowings, respectively.
Non-banking sources charged 13.5 percent for previous two-week borrowings and 15 percent for one-month loans.

The central bank calculated its kuna mid-rates for Saturday and Monday weaker at 6.1898 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5670 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
